classifications.rationale: This segment only recites statutory authorities, factors, notice requirements, and timing rules; it contains no presidential act or direction.
classifications.evidence: Section 502(d) of the Trade Act (19 U.S.C. 2462(d)) authorizes the President to withdraw, suspend, or limit the application of duty-free treatment under the GSP

classifications.rationale: This is a recital of statutory considerations and authorities, not an exercise of those authorities or a direction to an agency.
classifications.evidence: Section 502(a)(1) of the Trade Act (19 U.S.C. 2462(a)(1)) authorizes the President to designate countries as beneficiary developing countries for purposes of the GSP.

classifications.rationale: The President makes the substantive statutory determination that Malaysia no longer warrants GSP treatment and fixes the termination's effective date; the legal consequence follows from this present presidential determination.
classifications.evidence: it is appropriate to terminate the designation of Malaysia as a beneficiary developing country for purposes of the GSP effective January 1, 1997

classifications.rationale: The President determines the termination of Malaysia's ASEAN designation and competitive-need waivers, substantive changes to its GSP treatment, with later tariff-schedule modifications reflecting those acts.
classifications.evidence: to terminate any waivers of the competitive need limits granted to Malaysia

classifications.rationale: This fragment merely cites statutory authority and performs no action.
classifications.evidence: Pursuant to section 502(e) of the Trade Act

classifications.rationale: The President makes the statutory high-income determination that, under the cited statute, triggers termination of the countries' beneficiary designations at the prescribed later date.
classifications.evidence: I have determined that Cyprus, Aruba, Macau, the Netherlands Antilles, Greenland, and the Cayman Islands meet the definition of a "high income" country

classifications.rationale: The President directly terminates specified countries' preferential GSP treatment effective on a stated date; later implementation is ministerial.
classifications.evidence: I am terminating the preferential treatment under the GSP

classifications.rationale: The President makes the substantive determination to suspend part of Pakistan's GSP benefits under the cited statutory authority, with the affected articles implemented through the tariff schedule.
classifications.evidence: I have determined that it is appropriate to suspend some of Pakistan's GSP benefits

classifications.rationale: The President determines that Pakistan will lose preferential tariff treatment for specified articles on a fixed date and also acts to correct beneficiary-country names in the tariff schedule.
classifications.evidence: Pakistan will no longer receive preferential tariff treatment under the GSP with respect to certain eligible articles effective July 1, 1996

classifications.rationale: The President makes the substantive statutory determination to disregard competitive-need limitations and restore GSP treatment to qualifying articles; later schedule changes implement that determination.
classifications.evidence: to disregard section 503(c)(2)(A)(i)(II) of the Trade Act with respect to certain eligible articles

classifications.rationale: The President determines which countries are to lose or receive least-developed beneficiary status, a substantive eligibility designation implemented in the ensuing tariff-schedule modification.
classifications.evidence: Botswana and Western Samoa should be deleted from the list of least-developed beneficiary developing countries and Angola, Ethiopia, Madagascar, Zaire, and Zambia should be added

classifications.rationale: The President presently modifies the Harmonized Tariff Schedule through incorporated annexes, thereby changing beneficiary designations and preferential tariff treatment.
classifications.evidence: the HTS is modified as provided in Annex I to this proclamation

classifications.rationale: This is an internal delegation of a presidential notification function to the United States Trade Representative, not itself a change to a country's GSP status.
classifications.evidence: I delegate to the United States Trade Representative the powers granted to me in section 502(f)(2) of the Trade Act

classifications.rationale: The segment inseparably combines housekeeping supersession of inconsistent prior directives with a self-executing rule governing when substantive tariff modifications apply to imported articles.
classifications.evidence: The modifications to the HTS made in paragraphs (1) through (4) of this proclamation shall be effective
